newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union to seek FERC approval for merger.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union to seek FERC approval for merger.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co said Monday it planned to apply to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for approval of its merger with Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO).
"We have to apply to the (New York) state Public Service Commission and FERC," said a Brooklyn Union spokesman.
The two utilities announced Sunday that they had agreed to merge to form a $4.0 billion electric and gas holding company.
An FERC spokeswoman said Monday it was unclear whether the companies needed the federal commission's approval.
"Nobody here knows enough (about the merger plan) to say with certainty" whether it requires a nod from FERC, she said.

Under the Federal Power Act, if an electric utility is going to dispose of, sell or acquire facilities which fall under FERC's jurisdiction, such as interstate transmission lines, then the utility has to seek FERC approval.
The U.S. commission issued a new merger policy two weeks ago, aiming to simplify its merger approval process.

The policy was designed to be flexible enough to address combinations of electric utilities as well as growing trend of mergers of electric and natural gas companies, such as Brooklyn Union and LILCO, the commission said.
